example_summary: XYZ Ltd. takes over a sole-proprietor business via a sale deed, undertaking an overriding charge to pay ₹ 15,000 p.a. to the wife of the sole-proprietor.
source_provision:
### Statutory Framework: Diversion vs. Application of Income

| Doctrine Aspect | Diversion of Income by Overriding Title | Application of Income |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Source Attachment** | Obligation attaches directly to the **source of income** itself | Obligation arises **after** the income has accrued or reached the assessee |
| **Taxability** | Excluded from the total income of the recipient/holder | Included in total income; no deduction allowed unless specifically provided |
| **Judicial Precedent** | *Jit & Pal X-Rays (P.) Ltd. v. CIT* (All HC) | General statutory provisions of Section 4 and Section 5 |


> [!IMPORTANT] Core Legal Test: The Allahabad High Court established that when a going concern is acquired under a sale deed with an integrated overriding charge on net profits in favor of a third party, the charge binds the source itself.


> [!WARNING] Statutory Trap: Mere directions to apply profits after they are earned do not create an overriding charge and will fail to reduce the taxable business income of the assessee.

director.justification: The question revolves around whether an integrated overriding obligation under a sale deed constitutes diversion of income or application of income based on the judicial precedent of Jit & Pal X-Rays (P.) Ltd. v. CIT.
director.visual_metaphor: A main income stream pipe fitted with a pre-reservoir diversion tap that redirects funds directly to a third party before reaching the recipient's pool.
